sources.news_title: Entire US govt will fit in palm of your hand: Donald Trump launches America.gov portal - The Tribune
sources.text:
Washington DC [US], September 30 (ANI): United States President Donald Trump on Tuesday (local time) launched America.gov, describing the new federal portal as "one of the most revolutionary product launches of all time," designed to put the entire machinery of the federal government directly into citizens' hands.
Speaking at the unveiling of the government platform, President Trump said the initiative represents far more than a standard digital upgrade.
"We are launching today something that is not just simply a website; it's one of the most revolutionary product launches of all time, a restoration of America's founding promise, and it's a reinvention of your government for the 21st Century and beyond. For our entire lives, we've become used to a government so big, it makes the citizen feel very, very small — but with America.gov, the entire U.S. government will fit in the palm of your hand," Trump said.
The announcement came alongside an Executive Order signed by the US President directing federal agencies to integrate their public-facing operations onto the platform.
The platform, officially unveiled alongside US Chief Design Officer Joe Gebbia, is envisioned as a secure, intelligent, single digital point of entry for Americans to access federal government information using plain language and modern Super Intelligence (SI) technology.
Rather than forcing users to navigate a maze of disparate agency websites, the portal allows citizens to get verified answers immediately. In the coming months, essential services such as passport renewals and Medicare enrollment will be rolled out directly on the platform.
Alongside the unveiling, President Trump signed an Executive Order directing federal agencies to integrate their covered public-facing services—specifically those handling more than 100,000 users annually—into America.gov, while excluding national-security-sensitive services and tax filing under the Internal Revenue Service.
According to the White House, the reform is aimed at eliminating bureaucracy and saving Americans the estimated 10 billion hours spent every year dealing with federal paperwork. (ANI)

sources.news_title: Trump Launches America.gov Portal
sources.text:
President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Tuesday directing the creation of America.gov as a single online entry point for people seeking federal information and services.
The order, titled “Streamlining Access To Government Services Through America.Gov,” establishes a secure, conversational, AI-powered platform intended to serve as a “unified digital front door to the Federal Government.”
Users will be able to sign in, ask questions in plain language, search thousands of federal databases, and — when technically available and authorized — complete eligible federal transactions without navigating multiple agency websites. Trump signed the order at a White House event also featuring AI and tech executives.
“Advances in technology now make possible a fundamentally different relationship between the people and the Federal Government, defined by simplicity, speed, accuracy, security, and respect for the individual,” the executive order states. “The same spirit of American innovation that can accelerate scientific discovery can also help Americans complete essential interactions with the Federal Government. … America.gov will enable the Federal Government to do its own paperwork so that the American people may get on with their lives.”
At an event announcing the site, Trump said, “With America.gov the federal government no longer stands in your way, it only stands at your service. We’re simplifying it. We’re glamorizing it. We’re making it what it should be,” Politico reported.
America.Gov To Connect Federal Services
The executive order directs the General Services Administration (GSA), working with the National Design Studio and the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), to establish and operate America.gov. The National Design Studio was created by an August 2025 executive order and is led by Airbnb cofounder Joe Gebbia.
The platform is intended to provide access to public-facing federal services that serve more than 100,000 users over a 12-month period and can be accessed or applied for online. Tax filing services provided by the Internal Revenue Service are excluded, along with services provided by the Department of War and elements of the Intelligence Community. The OMB director may modify the definition of covered services through a memorandum.
America.gov is expected to integrate with Login.gov, which will serve as its authentication system. The website draws from official U.S. government resources and currently functions as a chatbot that answers questions and points users to federal services. Officials said more transactions, including passport applications, are expected to be completed on the platform as agencies integrate with it.
Agencies Given Integration Requirements
Federal agencies must identify which of their services qualify as covered services and integrate those offerings with America.gov in a secure and privacy-preserving manner. Agencies are directed to make existing public application programming interfaces, dashboards, and digital forms accessible through the new platform. They must also complete Login.gov integration and provide the GSA and OMB with ongoing information about service usage and performance.
The OMB director has 90 days from the order’s date to issue implementation guidance to federal agencies. One account of the directive indicates agencies are to integrate public-facing services into the platform on a timeline tied to that guidance.
Existing Service Options To Remain
America.gov is not intended to eliminate existing ways of obtaining federal services. In-person, telephone, mail, and agency-specific online services are to remain available. Agencies will retain custody and control of their records, systems, and statutory responsibilities.
The order calls for personal information to be protected through data minimization, secure authentication, and authorization practices consistent with federal law. Creating a unified access point is not to result in a centralized federal system of records about Americans. Information protected by law must not be disclosed, and the order does not authorize access to an agency’s records about an individual except as permitted by applicable law.
Implementation Will Take Time
The executive order establishes the framework for America.gov but leaves agencies to carry out the integration process. Implementation is subject to applicable law and the availability of federal funding. The GSA and OMB will receive ongoing data on the performance and use of covered services as agencies connect them to the platform.
More federal services are expected to be added over the coming months as agencies begin to integrate with America.gov.

sources.news_title: Trump's own AI-powered website confirms he lost the 2020 election: 'Finally, a straight answer from someone in the Trump administration'
sources.text:
President Trump’s new AI-powered website, America.gov, is currently providing clear confirmation that Joseph R. Biden Jr. won the 2020 presidential election, The Hill reports. This result directly contradicts the claims made by the 47th president himself.
When users utilize the site’s search bar to ask about the 2020 election, the AI provides a definitive answer. It states, “Joseph R. Biden Jr. won the 2020 U.S. presidential election. According to the National Archives, he received 306 electoral votes to Donald J. Trump’s 232. A majority of 270 was needed.”
The AI backs up this claim by citing official data from the National Archives and the Federal Election Commission. These links lead users directly to the government records that outline the final results.
When you ask similar questions, the system consistently pulls from these same official sources
Sen. Adam Schiff, who served as the lead impeachment manager during the first impeachment trial in January 2020, took notice of this discrepancy. He tested the search bar himself and shared the results on X. He wrote, “Finally, a straight answer from someone in the Trump administration,” while attaching a screenshot that showed the AI confirming the 2020 election outcome.
Trump officially launched the website on Tuesday at an event held at the Andrew W. Mellon Auditorium in Washington, D.C. He has been calling the platform the ultimate product. The site is a direct result of an executive order signed in August 2025, which aims to make the public experience with government services more effective and respectful of people’s time.
During the launch event, Trump explained his vision for the site. He said, “Instead of forcing citizens to search through the endless maze of tens of thousands of terrible government websites and rules, and more than 10,000 forms … you’ll now have one front door for every single question.” He also noted that the website is designed so that it cannot be hacked, at least in theory.
While the AI has provided these specific answers, there have been some changes to how the tool operates. Some users have reported that the system began refusing to answer certain political inquiries, including questions about the 2020 presidential election, climate change, and mentions of Donald Trump in the Department of Justice files regarding Jeffrey Epstein.
In these cases, the AI simply states that it does not answer political inquiries. However, when other tests were conducted, the website still provided thorough answers with direct links to official government pages.
A White House official mentioned that the site will continue to evolve. The official stated that the website will be updated with more resources and “the most accurate information from the federal government.” They also added, “The President and Administration have been clear about issues surrounding the 2020 election, issues that have been documented by John Solomon and the White House Government Transparency Task Force.”
The website currently serves as an information hub, but it’s slated to become much more functional in the future. According to the site’s description, users can expect to complete various applications, forms, and renewals like passport applications and Medicare enrollment by early 2027.

sources.news_title: The US Government Just Launched an AI Chatbot
sources.text:
AI is virtually everywhere in 2026; that now includes U.S. government websites. On Tuesday, the Trump administration launched "America.gov," a new website that uses AI to answer questions about the government. While the experience currently feels like ChatGPT running U.S. government-themed instructions, the plan is for America.gov to eventually let you take action as well.
What is America.gov?
America.gov "combines" the nearly 30,000 websites under the umbrella of the U.S. government into one set of sources. Rather than invite you to browse those tens of thousands of pages to answer your questions, that dataset serves as the basis for the site's proprietary chatbot. You ask the chatbot a question about the U.S. government, and the AI sifts through those websites to generate an answer. It's like ChatGPT, but if the model only had access to U.S. government websites and sources.
You could ask the site how to replace your Social Security card, renew your passport, or register to vote in your state. You could ask for information on changing your address with the USPS, when Medicare open enrollment dates are, or upload a PDF of a government form for assistance. The site says any personal information will be automatically removed, though the privacy policy clarifies that it "will make a best-effort attempt in your browser to remove any private details using Rampart (an open-source classifier system to detect some types of PII, such as Social Security Numbers, phone numbers, email addresses, and credit card numbers)."
The website currently supports three languages—English, Spanish, and French—as well as voice commands, if you prefer speaking to your chatbots rather than typing to them. You don't need an account to use it, nor is there a fee or subscription, and there are no ads.
What America.gov might be able to do in the future
In its current form, America.gov is a simple chatbot. But the site has bold claims for future features. Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced plans to let users apply for and renew their passports directly through the site, including a dynamic progress tracker to keep tabs on your documents. Other future abilities could include enrolling in Medicare or finding a job with the federal government.
But as with all claims, take these with a grain of salt. The government says these features are coming in early 2027, but this is a tall order for such a project. A single website that lets you complete complex government processes with the simplicity of a chatbot sounds great, but it would need to be accurate and reliable for all possible tasks and functions. It would certainly take significant proof of security and dependability for me to trust such a program with renewing my passport or helping me enroll in health care.
America.gov is full of ironies
It's impossible to discuss America.gov without acknowledging the administration that is spearheading the project. One would assume that an AI-powered government website developed by this administration would be biased towards Trump and his many falsehoods. And yet, the tool is astoundingly neutral, to the point where I can only imagine how frustrated Trump would be by some of these answers.
The first question many tested America.gov with was "Who won the 2020 election?" Donald Trump famously and frequently says that the election was stolen from him, but his new website plainly states that Joseph R. Biden Jr. won. The bot does sometimes tie the answer to the electoral count, stating that Biden won 306 votes to Trump's 232, but I was surprised to see "Joseph R. Biden Jr. won the 2020 presidential election under the official Electoral College count" as an answer on this site.
The site will also tell you that Donald Trump was president when diesel prices hit their highest historic price ($6.529 per gallon as of Sept. 21, 2026.), and that prices are high, in part, due to "military action" affecting the Staight of Hormuz. It will also say that grocery prices were higher in August than they were a year ago, which contradicts Trump's claims that prices have come down under his term.
Of course, Trump-influenced information that appears on official government sites will appear here. Ask it what the body of water that abuts Texas is called, and it will say the Gulf of America, formerly the Gulf of Mexico. Ask it what lake borders Toronto, Canada, and the bot will say Lake America, formerly Lake Ontario. In both cases, it will refer to the executive orders that changed those names.
Typically, I'd be worried about an AI tool hallucinating its answers and providing incorrect information to users. That's still a concern here, of course. But by creating a chatbot that only pulls information from official government sources, Trump has inadvertently created an official government fact-checker. And unless Trump starts injecting these sites with the same falsehoods he tells in interviews and on Truth Social, America.gov may be a reasonably reliable source of information.

sources.news_title: Trump's new AI website America.gov said Biden won 2020—then the White House made the chatbot stop answering
sources.text:
The Trump administration has lauded its revamped website America.gov as a way to simplify Americans’ access to information and services scattered across a plethora of agency sites, but President Donald Trump probably won’t like some of the answers his new site says are sourced from government information.
Asking the site — which says it’s sourced via artificial intelligence from “official government sources” — questions about who won the 2020 election or about the name of the federal department that operates out of the Pentagon yields answers contrary to those Trump himself frequently proclaims.
As Trump was still speaking at Tuesday’s launch event, however, the site began modifying its answers. Asked again about the 2020 election, it replied that it couldn’t answer “political questions,” a response it also gave to inquiries about whether Trump had been impeached or convicted of felony charges.
The Associated Press asked about:
The 2020 presidential election
“Official federal sources do not show that widespread fraud changed the 2020 presidential election outcome. Isolated election crimes did occur and have been prosecuted.”
Since Trump, a Republican, lost the 2020 election to Democrat Joe Biden, he has repeatedly falsely claimed that victory was “stolen” from him and asserted that widespread fraud occurred. Repeated audits and recounts found no significant fraud in the presidential election, and Trump’s own administration said the election was clean.
Trump running for president in 2028
“The 22nd Amendment says that no person shall be elected President more than twice. Donald J. Trump has already been elected twice (2016 and 2024). I am not giving legal advice.”
Trump has frequently suggested he wants to seek a third term, posting about mounting another campaign, donning 2028 caps and discussing ways to make it happen — even as he’s acknowledged the Constitution prohibits it. He had only been back in the White House for a couple of months when he told NBC News, “There are methods which you could” use to seek a third term.
The Pentagon
“The Pentagon is the headquarters of the Department of Defense.”
Last year, Trump signed an executive order aimed at rebranding the Department of Defense as the Department of War, complaining that the Department of Defense’s name was “woke.”
Human action as cause of climate change
“Federal climate-science pages say recent warming is largely from human greenhouse-gas emissions, mainly burning fossil fuels. Earth’s climate has also changed for natural reasons over long periods.”
Trump, who has called climate change a “hoax,” previously issued an executive order that directed the Environmental Protection Agency to submit a report on “the legality and continuing applicability” of the endangerment finding. Conservatives and some congressional Republicans have long sought to undo what they consider overly restrictive and economically damaging rules to limit greenhouse gases that cause global warming.
Presidential salaries
The chatbot said that “some presidents have declined to keep that pay,” mentioning Trump but listing George Washington, Herbert Hoover and John F. Kennedy as refusing their salaries before Trump.
During his remarks Tuesday, Trump, a real estate mogul who took in about $1.2 billion from various crypto holdings last year, said he was the first U.S. president to forgo a salary, something that he has said before.
___
Kinnard reported from Columbia, S.C.

sources.news_title: Trump Announces Launch of Government AI-Powered Chatbot Allowing Users to Research Public Services
sources.text:
by Kevin Killough
President Donald Trump on Tuesday launched America.gov, a government chatbot powered by artificial intelligence. It will allow the public to research government services.
“This kind of innovation in government is just a preview of what is possible with super intelligence,” Trump said, the Washington Post reported.
Initially, the website will help users search for information across government websites. Later, the goal is for the website to help people enroll in government programs, such as Medicare.
While many Democrats in Congress are pressing for greater regulation of the AI industry, Trump used the announcement of the launch to assure the public the risks are being exaggerated.
“We do not surrender to fears about what technologies will do to us. We decide that those technologies will do for us some very, very incredible things,” Trump said.
The launch was part of a day-long event featuring Cabinet members and tech executives. AI executives are scheduled to meet with Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La.
Joe Gebbia, the chief design officer of the United States and architect of the new website, which is the result of a partnership between Google’s Gemini and SpaceXAI’s Grok, told Fox News on Monday that it’s a “concierge to navigate government.”
“Don’t think of it as a website, it’s more of a conversation that you start with the government to try to get access to the answers you need,” Gebbia said.
United States Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum said the president “is unleashing American innovation to modernize the federal government.”
“Under his leadership, we are building a more modern and effective government that delivers better results and works for the people it serves,” he noted.
Veteran Affairs Secretary Doug Collins said, “Government shouldn’t require a degree in bureaucracy to navigate it.”
“America.gov gives Americans a new place to find information and services across the federal government,” he noted.
– – –
Kevin Killough is a reporter for Just the News. Zachery Schmidt is the digital editor of The Star News Network and contributed to this story.

The central feature is a chatbot that answers questions in a conversational style and directs visitors towards government services. The site combines this with a search function intended to make it easier to find the relevant agency or information.
The aim is to reduce the amount of navigating users must do across government websites before reaching the service they need.

Rubio said the website would 'make life better, easier, for normal Americans.' He described a passport application process that people would be able to complete online from next year, including taking and uploading the required photograph with a mobile phone.
That timetable puts the full passport application service beyond the launch. The distinction matters for anyone arriving at the site expecting to complete the process immediately, even as the search tool helps users find government information.

sources.text:
What to know about America.gov, the Trump administration’s new AI-driven services website
By Adam Cancryn, CNN
(CNN) — The Trump administration thinks the federal bureaucracy is way too complex for Americans to navigate — and it believes that artificial intelligence can help.
President Donald Trump on Tuesday unveiled America.gov, a government website meant to serve as a one-stop shop for people trying to accomplish basic tasks like renewing a passport, enrolling in Medicare or applying for disaster relief.
The site, which launched with some basic functions ahead of a full rollout next year, is designed to serve as an AI-powered guide through the thicket of government agencies that Trump officials pledged would ultimately save people a whole lot of frustration.
“You’ll now have one front door for every single question,” Trump said during a speech at the America.gov launch event. “A digital home built around your time, your life.”
In a slew of presentations on Tuesday, Cabinet secretaries showed off hypothetical ways to use the site, touting its ability to accomplish tasks — which traditionally required hours of navigating multiple federal websites — in a few clicks.
But the real test will come when Americans begin using the site en masse, especially as the administration races to hit its early 2027 deadline for delivering on its loftiest promises.
Here’s what we know about America.gov so far:
How it’s supposed to work
The administration’s new initiative aims to allow Americans to access dozens of federal websites through a single point, making America.gov akin to a search tool that pulls information from across the government.
And in the same way that people increasingly use AI models like ChatGPT or Google Gemini to compile information and provide customized answers, Trump officials claimed that America.gov would be able to do the same for people’s interactions with the federal government.
Enrolling in Medicare, for example, will become a matter of typing the request into the America.gov AI tool and following its step-by-step instructions. The same goes for applying to a government job — the new tool will now let people upload their resume directly to the site — or answering questions about federal benefits, publicly available documents or other necessities that fall under the federal government’s vast umbrella.
“Our vision is that one day, this type of convenience and simplicity will be across every government service,” said Joseph Gebbia, who leads the government’s National Design Studio.
What Americans can do and when
Trump and his top officials on Tuesday stressed some of the more ambitious capabilities tied to America.gov, such as applying for a passport in a few easy steps.
But the reality is that the most advanced actions won’t be available until some point in 2027, raising questions about how long it will take for the administration to revamp the way the people interact with the government’s websites.
The current version of America.gov can only do “answers,” Gebbia said, essentially serving as a sleek version of a traditional search engine that returns only information available across the federal ecosystem. So while it can lay out the steps required to renew a passport, or change your last name after getting married, it can’t do those tasks for you.
Trump officials say that will change in the first months of 2027, when they roll out more advanced features that enable AI to effectively complete complex actions on your behalf. That will be the case with renewing a passport, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in his presentation, as he walked through a simulation of a future America.gov site that allows an applicant to submit their personal information, upload a photo and then track the passport’s approval and shipment.
Why now
Across the rollout, Trump and his aides repeatedly marveled that prior administrations had not sought to simplify Americans’ main source of interaction with their government — one widely seen as irritating and time-consuming.
Trump during his speech said officials had been building America.gov since the beginning of his term. But the timing of the rollout just before the midterms also serves a political purpose, attempting to show how Trump is improving Americans’ lives at a time when polls show most voters believe his agenda hasn’t delivered for them.
“Somebody said it’s going to be the single biggest thing you’ve done in government,” Trump said. “I said, ‘I don’t think so, but it’s damn good.’”
The initiative also represents an effort to demonstrate tangible benefits of AI at a time when most Americans are deeply skeptical of the technology — and by extension, questioning the administration’s close embrace of the fast-growing AI industry.
The America.gov rollout came just hours before Trump was due to meet with top tech executives to discuss some of those concerns, including the slew of recent security breaches caused by AI that have prompted even some of the top tech companies to float the need to slow down development of their models.
Trump again brushed off those concerns during his presentation, pointing to the new federal site as evidence that AI is capable of delivering far more benefits compared with its potential drawbacks — and making the case for continuing to press the accelerator regardless of the growing calls for caution.

“Everything the internet has transformed, there’s one thing that hasn’t caught up: the everyday experience of the government,” said Gebbia, who co-founded Airbnb and was tapped by Trump to lead the newly created National Design Studio in August 2025.
Speaking at an event that had the look and feel of an Apple Worldwide Developers Conference, Gebbia demonstrated various aspects of America.gov, the opening page of which reads: “Hello, America. Whatever you need from government, start here.”

White House launches AI-powered ‘America.gov’ digital front door
The president signed an executive order at the event requiring agencies to integrate many of their services with the new website.
The Trump administration launched an artificial intelligence-powered one-stop shop for citizens interested in federal services and information on Tuesday with the help of former Department of Government Efficiency employees.
The website currently allows users to ask a chatbot questions about everything from qualifying for Medicare to finding a job to renewing a passport, without ever creating an account. Users receive AI-generated answers derived only from official federal sources.
America.gov, which sifts through 29,000 websites to pull responses, states it is free to use and “never includes ads, and keeps your privacy protected.” It’s unclear what large language models power the chatbot.
Phase two of America.gov, which is set for early 2027, will allow Americans to apply for, enroll in and track progress of benefits such as Social Security directly within the chatbot.
“One of the most revolutionary product launches of all time. It really is,” President Donald Trump said at a launch event in Washington, D.C., on Tuesday. “We’re putting power and control back into the hands of the people, right where it belongs,” he added.
At the event, Trump signed an executive order mandating that agencies ensure public-facing services integrate directly with America.gov as soon as possible.
The order states that services integrating with America.gov will “include public-facing federal services that serve more than 100,000 users in a 12-month period and can be accessed or applied for online. Tax filing services provided by the Internal Revenue Service and national-security-sensitive services provided by the Department of War and the Intelligence Community are excluded.”
The order also directs the head of the Office of Management and Budget to issue guidance to agencies on implementing their covered services into America.gov.
America.gov does not include web-tracking technologies, save conversations or use specific locations to share information, according to its privacy page.
The National Design Studio, a Trump administration creation that includes former DOGE employees, designed and engineered America.gov. The General Services Administration is operating the website amid a major shakeup to its web design system staff.
Approximately 40 million people visit government websites each day, Joe Gebbia, the National Design Studio’s chief design officer, said at the event.
Under phase two, Americans will be able to upload and send marriage certificates to federal agencies of their choice through the chatbot, according to a presentation Gebbia shared at the launch event.
Americans will also be able to use login.gov to digitally verify their identities and send that information to agencies such as the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, the Social Security Administration and the Department of Veterans Affairs, according to a presentation CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz shared at the event.
Oz touted America.gov’s ability to show verified users the locations of doctors near them who accept Medicare and enables them to schedule medical appointments. The website also allows users to pull information about drugs they take, compare medication costs and find local pharmacies that carry the medications.
Oz argued the new website will be more useful than informational Medicare packets CMS sends Americans each year, costing approximately $100 million. Oz previously flirted with using AI to help Medicare beneficiaries find health plans and doctors.
“For 165 million Americans, you get Medicare, Medicaid, Obamacare. We want these systems eventually to integrate and be able to help so many Americans,” Oz said of America.gov.
Oz told reporters he is pushing for CMS to be as transparent “as possible” about Medicare plans highlighted on America.gov and “make it hard” for insurance companies “to game” information.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio showed that Americans can apply for a passport after signing in with login.gov. The service will launch in December 2026, according to a presentation Rubio gave at the event. The State Department already has an online passport renewal platform that has issued millions of passports.
“By the end of 2027, our goal is for the vast majority of Americans to be able to apply for a passport or passport card on America.gov,” Rubio said.
Rubio also unveiled the 2028 U.S. passport, which he said the State Department created alongside the National Design Studio.
Two civic technologists cautioned that America.gov has not yet proven itself to be the watershed website that Trump administration officials heralded.
“This isn't any big leap forward over the other ‘one-stop shops’ that have been tried before. What remains to be seen is how it could be integrated with any agency program,” Mikey Dickerson, former administrator of the U.S. Digital Service and senior advisor to Democratic-aligned Tech Viaduct, told Nextgov/FCW.
“My first read [of America.gov] is that like many other [National Design Studio] websites, the real functionality is ‘coming soon’ — I tested a VA disability claim and it directs me to the VA site. It claims to be able to do that in 2027, but that’s a significantly heavier lift than building an LLM wrapper,” Christopher Whitaker, executive director of the Alliance of Civic Technologists and a Tech Viaduct contributor, posted on social media.
Other top Trump administration officials, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, General Services Administrator Edward Forst, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and former Federal Chief Information Officer Greg Barbaccia, attended the launch event.
Private sector leaders, including former DOGE leader Elon Musk and NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, are set to speak Tuesday afternoon.
Trump thanked Musk for “initially envision[ing] the transformation of government with technology” during his remarks, despite squabbling with the former DOGE leader in 2025.
Trump argued that America.gov highlights the need for the SAVE America Act, a federal bill requiring voters to provide photo ID at the time of voting that has stalled in Congress.
Trump said he will soon sign an executive order changing the name of AI to “super intelligence,” a new term he has recently coined; he claimed that Chinese President Xi Jinping supports the renaming. The America.gov order Trump signed refers to AI as super intelligence.
“We don't want to hear artificial because it's not artificial. It's very powerful. It's very brilliant,” Trump said.
The Washington Sun first reported on plans for America.gov earlier this month.

After originally confirming that Trump’s name is in the Epstein files, that Democrat Joe Biden beat him in the 2020 election and that climate change is largely human-caused, it subsequently refused to answer the questions, saying it didn’t answer political inquiries.
Meanwhile, former Justice Department special counsel Jack Smith, who brought two federal indictments against Trump, told lawmakers Tuesday that he “will not be silenced by continued threats of prosecution” from the Trump administration and that he believes the rule of law is being threatened like never before. Smith’s hearing before the Senate is expected to focus on his team’s access to GOP lawmakers’ phone records when prosecutors were investigating Trump’s efforts to overturn the results of the 2020 election.
Here's the latest:
White House releases self-policing AI pledge that Trump says is ‘morally binding’
The president signed an executive order after holding a White House lunch meeting with top industry leaders. It mostly focuses on Trump’s insistence that artificial intelligence be called “super intelligence.”
But Trump said the document would work with industry leaders to keep AI safe for users while also not limiting innovation in the field.
The president said that officials were already “seeing tremendous self-policing” around ensuring AI doesn’t become too powerful for its own good. And he said his administration may create a 10-person committee charged with overseeing the AI industry.
Key Democratic senator criticizes Hegseth’s planned cuts of generals
Sen. Jack Reed, a Rhode Island Democrat and ranking member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, said eliminating senior leadership positions must be done in consultation with Congress.
Pentagon officials say Hegseth plans to announce in an address Wednesday that the military needs to carry out a 20% total decrease to the roughly 800 flag and general officer positions by Jan. 1, 2027.
Reed warned that the planned cuts “should alarm every American.”
“Congress has been clear with the Secretary that he must consult this body and explain his reasoning for senior officer removals and promotion holds. To date, we have not received satisfactory answers,” Reed said in a statement.
“Our military is conducting major operations around the world, and the force is already under strain,” he added. “Eliminating senior positions and leaders now will add to that strain and disrupt command when continuity matters most.”
Hegseth set to announce more job cuts for generals
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is planning to announce further cuts to the number of generals and admirals in an address set for Wednesday.
According to Pentagon officials, Hegseth will direct all the military services to double the 10% reduction that he ordered last spring to the roughly 800 flag and general officer positions, making it a 20% total decrease to be completed by Jan. 1, 2027.
Trump or Hegseth already have fired or pushed to retire more than two dozen military leaders since taking office, including the Army’s top uniformed officer, Gen. Randy George.
Hegseth will make the announcement in a speech to troops at the Marine Corps Base Quantico in Virginia, the second year in a row he will deliver what the Pentagon is calling his “State of the Force” address.
Fox News earlier reported the new reductions.
Senate Republican blocks Democratic resolution disapproving of taxpayer-funded ads promoting Trump
New Hampshire Sen. Maggie Hassan went to the Senate floor on Tuesday and tried to pass a resolution by unanimous consent that said it is the “sense of the Senate” that the campaign-style ads promoting President Donald Trump should not be funded by taxpayers.
Political messages “should not come at the cost of hard-earned American tax dollars,” Hassan said.
Wyoming Sen. Cynthia Lummis objected, comparing the ads to government public service announcements of the past, like anti-drug campaigns and pro-vaccination messages during the coronavirus pandemic. “I don’t recall a single Democrat rushing to the floor to object to any of them,” Lummis said.
Hassan responded that “people know the difference between a PSA and a political ad.”
Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said this week that he believes the ads should not be funded by taxpayers.
Trump says he’ll do a 32-day campaign tour ahead of the midterms
Despite the president’s approval ratings sinking to near historic lows ahead of Election Day in November, Trump maintained of Republican candidates around the country, “They all want me to go” and help out in their races.
He said he’d be launching a 32-day blitz to the midterm elections that would begin on Thursday with a trip to Texas.
Trump added that he’d also be going to Ohio and “all different places.”
All of Trump’s planned stops haven’t yet been made public, but he is set to visit Alabama on Friday and Nebraska on Monday.
Some top Republican elected officials and candidates have begun to distance themselves from Trump, calling for an end to the war in Iran or softening of his immigration policies. But the president believes the best way he can help the GOP is personally rallying his “Make America Great Again” base in different areas.
Trump calls Google CEO a ‘monster’ — in a good way
Trump introduced Google CEO Sundar Pichai to reporters in an unusual way.
“This guy is a monster, and nobody knows,” Trump said approvingly. Pichai described the voluntary AI agreement this way, using Trump’s new branding for artificial intelligence:
“We are signing up to a set of processes and controls like we do in other areas, like financial controls, in a company. And we are bringing those well-known best practices to the development of superintelligence,” Pichai told reporters.
The text of the new accord is not yet available. Here’s how Zuckerberg described it
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg told reporters at the White House that the new accord included “a set of principles and commitments around building robust internal controls and detecting if there are any issues with the technology.”
Zuckerberg, who had distanced his company from calls for a slowdown in AI, said the new agreement would be “coupled with multiple layers of auditing and controls, starting with internal risk review, external auditors and evaluators and agreeing that we’re going to have all of our boards of directors independently review the reports that come from the auditors.”
Trump says data centers are ‘absolutely beautiful’
The president has spent months defending tech companies building data centers around the country, even amid a growing backlash from voters on the right and the left.
He made the case again during his impromptu White House driveway question-and-answer session. But this time, Trump drew on his decades as a New York real estate developer and suggested that centers make very aesthetically pleasing buildings.
“By the way, I’m very good at real estate. Some of those buildings are absolutely beautiful,” Trump said. “They’re big and they’re, you know, big, strong, powerful buildings. But they’re beautiful and they add greatly to a community.”
Anthropic’s Amodei says AI safety mechanism still under discussion
One of the loudest voices on the risks of AI -- Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei -- said after the meeting that he thinks the industry can protect safety.
“But I think the technology has very real risks. And, you know, the mechanism, how we address those risks is still under discussion,” Amodei said during the White House driveway news conference.
Amodei had dinner with Trump on Sunday night and was part of Tuesday’s industry meeting.
Trump and AI leaders have signed a voluntary accord for reviews of artificial intelligence after White House meeting
President Donald Trump on Tuesday said that he and a large group of leaders of artificial intelligence companies had signed a voluntary accord that will include internal and external reviews of the technology during a meeting at the White House.
“I think I’m seeing tremendous self-policing. And they understand that they have to self-police,” Trump told reporters outside the West Wing.
Details of the accord were not immediately available.
Supreme Court lets quick deportations to third countries resume for now while it weighs Trump policy
The high court said Tuesday it will hear arguments on whether migrants must have a chance to object.
The order lifts for now an appeals court ruling. Federal attorneys said the lower court’s decision forced the cancellation of a deportation flight carrying about 70 people.
Under a series of often-secret agreements, Trump’s Republican administration has deported some 25,000 people to more than two dozen countries. The case comes amid a sweeping immigration crackdown by the Trump administration.
Trump praises AI self-regulation and data centers at White House tech luncheon
The president called his White House lunch meeting with top tech executives to discuss artificial intelligence “very productive” and said that those gathered were united in that “we love our country and we love the world, and we want to make sure it’s a safe place.”
Trump said the tech leaders were “the greatest, most brilliant people in the world,” but offered few details on what AI guardrails might have been discussed.
Instead he praised “self-regulation,” and added “we automatically have regulation with the Department of Justice, the FBI, all of that.”
The president repeated his defense of data centers being built around the country – despite them becoming increasingly unpopular.
Trump said the assembled tech leaders would work to make communities getting data centers happy by supplying oil and gas, making local education donations and providing tax revenue.
“Data centers are going to be very popular,” he said, because tech leaders “want to see communities that are safe and happy.”
Trump added: “Otherwise, they’ll be forced to go overseas or other locations.”
Alaska’s GOP senator says parties are divided over energy development in the state
Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan of Alaska said the war in Iran is temporary, but that a “forever war” is one Democrats wage against oil and gas projects in the state.
Sullivan is locked in a tight reelection campaign against Democrat Mary Peltola. He told The Associated Press that fuel costs are a “huge issue” and that people are hurting.
He said he’s focused on that through efforts that include supporting funding for a low-income heating assistance program and a temporary moratorium on U.S. exports of diesel until the war with Iran is over.
Many small rural communities accessible only by air or water rely on diesel for heat and electricity, with some shipments coming on barges before rivers freeze.
Sullivan spoke after a campaign rally in Juneau. He and Peltola have cast themselves as champions of oil and gas development in Alaska, even as Sullivan has tried to tie Peltola to national Democrats, who have often fought to restrict drilling.

A fighter jet that crashed into the Atlantic Ocean while landing on the aircraft carrier USS Dwight D. Eisenhower suffered a failure to the arresting gear that was designed to bring the jet to a halt after landing.
“Two Naval aviators assigned to Carrier Air Wing 3 subsequently ejected from their aircraft following an arresting gear failure and were promptly recovered by search-and-rescue personnel,” the Navy said in a statement released Tuesday.
According to the Navy, the jet was a E/A-18G Growler that was assigned to Electronic Attack Squadron 130, also known as the “Zappers.”
Eight sailors, including the two aviators, were evaluated by medical personnel and five were flown off the ship for follow-on treatment.

The four-hour hearing before the Senate Judiciary Committee was marked by partisan squabbling over what Republicans have characterized as political prosecutions against Trump as he sought a return to the White House.
Smith repeatedly defended the work of his investigative team, telling lawmakers: “Anybody who has worked with me or knows me during the course of my career knows that I would not let politics play a role.”
The hearing came as Republicans have pushed for Smith to himself be prosecuted. Smith said he “will not be silenced by continued threats of prosecution from the president or others.”
GAO tells lawmakers that Trump can’t withhold more than $800 million
President Donald Trump is not permitted to withhold beyond Wednesday, the end of the fiscal year, more than $800 million in spending approved by Congress.
That’s according to a review from the Government Accountability Office that was sent to federal lawmakers and Vice President JD Vance on Tuesday and obtained by The Associated Press.
The president proposed rescinding spending from 11 appropriations accounts, using a rare and contested power to axe funding for immigrant services and diversity-focused initiatives.
But the GAO said federal law provides that funds proposed for rescission must be made available unless Congress completes action on a bill rescinding them.
“Any withholding of appropriated funds beyond their date of expiration, regardless of size, subverts both the constitutional process for enacting federal law and Congress’s constitutional power of the purse,” wrote the GAO’s general counsel.
US targets Iran’s military supply chain with new sanctions
The United States is targeting people and companies around the globe that it accuses of being financial facilitators or enablers of Iran’s military supply chain.
The Trump administration is pushing forward with economic warfare against Tehran at a time when renewed diplomacy between the two countries remains uncertain.
The latest action by the Treasury Department on Tuesday is part of the administration’s “Operation Economic Outcast” campaign, which is aimed at severing “critical financial lifelines” for the already heavily sanctioned Iranian government.
“Treasury will not tolerate any support to the regime and will continue to identify, expose, and isolate Iran’s enablers,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement.
Ten individuals and entities based in Iran, Hong Kong and Pakistan now face sanctions over accusations of procuring weapons and weapon components for Iran’s defense ministry as it fights its now seven-month war against the U.S.
EPA union sues Zeldin over termination of labor contract
A union representing thousands of employees at the Environmental Protection Agency is suing EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin over his termination of a collective bargaining agreement with workers.
The American Federation of Government Employees Council 238 says Zeldin’s action last year unlawfully stripped about 8,000 federal workers of protections that help them do their jobs, follow sound science and speak up without fear of retaliation.
Zeldin abruptly terminated the labor contract in August 2025, two months after 139 employees signed a “declaration of dissent” with his policies, saying they “undermine the EPA mission of protecting human health and the environment.”
EPA ultimately fired 20 employees who signed the dissent letter, and suspended 119 without pay, the union says. Of those disciplined, 110 were covered by the collective bargaining agreement.
The union called Zeldin’s action an attempt to silence workers and remove protections for employees who spoke out about political interference with the agency’s scientific work.
Tech industry leaders joining Trump, Vance, top Cabinet members for White House lunch focused on AI
The president is hosting a White House lunch on artificial intelligence in the face of growing calls for the government to establish guardrails that can help contain the technology.
Attendees include Dario Amodei of Anthropic, Nikesh Arora of Palo Alto Networks, Amazon chief Jeff Bezos, Greg Brockman of OpenAI, Brad Gerstner of Altimeter and Nvidia’s Jensen Huang.
Also on hand will be Tesla and Space X’s Elon Musk and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella.
Those industry leaders will join Trump and Vance, as well as House Speaker Mike Johnson, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles.
Trump to campaign in solidly red Nebraska with midterms looming
The president has repeatedly promised to travel to competitive areas around the country, even as his approval ratings sink and Republicans increasingly scramble to try and hold control of Congress after Election Day in November.
But Trump is instead holding a rally on Monday in Grand Island, in solidly red, south-central Nebraska.
The state has a competitive congressional race in Omaha, but where Trump is going is a different, GOP-held district and media market, with an election that isn’t expected to be close.
Trump’s trip could be an effort to counter Dan Osborn, an independent candidate running for Nebraska’s Senate seat against incumbent Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts.
But the president hitting Grand Island comes as the midterm map is full of Senate races in other states where Democrats have far better shots of flipping GOP seats.
GOP’s Schmitt appears to mix-up teams during Smith accusation
Republicans spent much of the Senate hearing trying to trip up Smith and impeach his credibility.
In one notable moment, Republican Sen. Eric Schmitt accused Smith of traveling to Atlanta and attending a game for the city’s NBA team — the Hawks — in February 2024 while Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis was facing scrutiny for her romantic relationship with a special prosecutor in the Georgia 2020 election case.
But it appeared Schmitt got his teams confused. Smith said he had actually been at a game that day for the University of Iowa Hawkeyes in Maryland.
America.gov changes politically thorny answers moments after launch
As it initially launched, the site’s question-and-answer function answered some political questions truthfully — noting correctly that Biden won the 2020 election and that Obama’s 2009 inaugural crowd was bigger than Trump’s in 2017.
Within moments, however, the site began modifying its answers.
After originally reporting that Biden won in 2020, it refused to answer the question subsequently, saying it didn’t answer political inquiries.
Same went for a question on crowd size at Obama’s inauguration versus Trump’s first one.
The site also offered more muddled answers on other things Trump frequently says that aren’t true — like the Strait of Hormuz being fully reopened to commercial traffic.

President Donald Trump rolled out his new AI-powered federal website, America.gov, Tuesday with a security guarantee — that he promptly admitted wasn't true.
Trump unveiled the site at the Andrew W. Mellon Auditorium in Washington alongside Elon Musk, administration officials and tech industry leaders. Bloomberg reported that Trump also signed an executive order directing every federal agency to integrate its public-facing systems with the new portal.

He added that Congress could "now can pass, in theory, The Save America Act because it takes the number one excuse away from them."
The SAVE America Act, which would require documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote and photo ID to cast a ballot in federal elections, passed the House in February but has stalled in the Senate. sources.news_title: Trump signs order creating America.gov as one-stop federal services portal
sources.text:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump on Tuesday signed an executive order establishing America.gov as a single online front door for federal information and many public services, directing agencies to bring high-volume programs onto one platform so Americans no longer have to hop among agency websites to complete routine government business.
The order instructs the General Services Administration, working with the National Design Studio and the Office of Management and Budget, to operate America.gov and integrate Login.gov as its sign-in system. Officials described the site as a “secure, intelligent, and service-oriented” entry point where a person can log in, ask questions in plain language, get answers, and, where legally and technically allowed, finish transactions without leaving the platform.
“The federal government no longer stands in your way and it stands only at your service, and that’s what we’re doing,” Trump said at the announcement. “We’re simplifying it, we’re glamorizing it, we’re making it what it should be.”
The White House said Americans spend about 10 billion hours a year on federal paperwork. The order argues that government has long been organized around agencies rather than the people who use them, forcing applicants to repeat information, interpret jargon and prove identity multiple times.
Covered services are defined as public-facing federal programs that serve more than 100,000 users in a 12-month period and can be accessed or applied for online. Tax filing through the Internal Revenue Service is excluded, as are services of the Department of War and the Intelligence Community. OMB may add or remove programs by memorandum.
Agency heads must identify covered services, connect existing public APIs, dashboards and digital forms to America.gov, complete Login.gov integration, and share usage and performance data with GSA and OMB. OMB has 90 days to issue implementation guidance.
The order says agencies will keep custody of their records, statutory duties and decision-making authority. It states that unifying access “does not create a centralized Federal system of records concerning the American people” and requires data minimization, secure authentication and Privacy Act protections. In-person, phone, mail and agency-specific websites remain available.
The White House said Americans can already ask questions on America.gov and receive current answers. Later this year, officials said, users should be able to complete tasks such as passport renewal and Medicare enrollment on the site. Trump said a name change after marriage, often a multi-agency slog, would be possible “right on the platform.”
“Instead of forcing citizens to search through the endless maze of tens of thousands of terrible government websites and rules, and more than 10,000 forms […] you’ll now have one front door for every single question,” he said. “Everything will be answered easily and quickly. A digital home built around your time and your life will save hours and hours, many hours, hundreds of hours, perhaps a year, depending on how much of that type of information you need.”
He credited Elon Musk for the underlying idea of using technology to remake government operations.
“I have to thank the man who initially envisioned the transformation of government through technology and brought us the talent to get the job done, and that’s Elon Musk,” Trump said.
Trump also tied the launch to election legislation, arguing the platform would undercut claims that proof of citizenship or a passport is too hard to obtain.
“With this, nobody can any longer complain about providing proof of citizenship or voter ID […] You can get everything now that you need in just one simple swipe,” he said. “Nobody will have any excuses. We must pass, and now can pass […] the SAVE America Act. It takes their number one excuse away from them.”
He said every federal agency would be directed to integrate public services with America.gov “as soon as possible,” predicting other countries would copy the model.
“It’s gonna save you tremendous time and gonna save you a lot of accuracy, it’s gonna save you from making a lot of mistakes,” he said. “It’s not even your fault. Some of it is so bad, so cumbersome, […] and sometimes you get in trouble.”
The White House framed America.gov as part of a broader efficiency push, citing earlier design work by the National Design Studio, reductions in veterans’ benefits backlogs, and other digital initiatives.

Trump Launches America.Gov Website Simplifying Access To Government Services
Authored by Travis Gillmore via The Epoch Times,
President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Sept. 29 directing all federal agencies to integrate services with a new website designed to make it easier for users to find information and interact with the government.
He described the tool as "one of the most revolutionary product launches of all time."
America.gov will serve as a landing page consolidating nearly 30,000 federal government websites into one chatbot, powered by SpaceX's Grok and Google's Gemini. The site allows users to ask questions and receive guidance about procuring services.
"The federal government no longer stands in your way, and it stands only at your service," Trump said.
"We're simplifying it. We're glamorizing it. We're making it what it should be."
Plans for full integration with more than 10,000 forms across agencies will provide opportunities for full-service enrollment, where visitors can "apply, enroll, and track progress directly in the chat," according to a statement on the new site.
Users will find a "front door" to the government replacing the "endless maze" of websites and regulations, according to the president.
"It's not just simply a website. It's a restoration of America's founding promises, and it's a reinvention of your government for the 21st century and beyond," Trump said. "We're putting power and control back into the hands of the people, right where it belongs."
Once complete, Americans can request replacement Social Security cards, apply for passports and name changes, and access countless other government services.
"And with this, nobody can any longer complain about providing proof of citizenship or voter ID," Trump said, while calling for lawmakers to pass the SAVE America Act, which would mandate proof of citizenship to register and IDs to vote. "They're always saying it's too complicated. It's not complicated anymore."
Privacy is built into the system, no login is required, the site does not track visitors, and no personal information or conversations are recorded, according to administration officials.
Preventing data leaks and hacks is a priority, Trump said during his address, noting rapid advancement in technology and potential threats while touting security precautions against any attempts to infiltrate the system.
Visitors can type queries into the text box, mirroring modern AI interfaces. The chatbot can also translate three spoken languages - English, Spanish, and French - with more additions coming soon.
While the technology is built on artificial intelligence platforms, the president is proposing a universal name change for the innovation, suggesting that super intelligence, or SI, is superior to the "artificial" alternative.
Airbnb co-founder Joe Gebbia, the nation's first chief design officer, revealed the website to the public in a product-demo style presentation at the Andrew Mellon Auditorium in the nation's capital.
"There was a time when Americans entered great public buildings to meet our government, and when they did, the spaces achieved a user experience unlike anything else," Gebbia said, noting the impact of architectural design and grand rooms that communicated "dignity and respect" to all who entered.
"America.gov carries that idea into the age of super intelligence to reimagine a government built around you that respects your time, that works for you, that we can be proud of as Americans."
Approximately 39 million Americans visit federal government websites every day, collectively spending more than 10 billion hours annually on government-related paperwork, according to administration officials.
The website is live as of Sept. 29, with more features expected in the coming months.

sources.news_title: Streamlining Access to Government Services Through America.gov
sources.text:
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered:
Section 1. Purpose. For generations, Americans seeking essential services from the Federal Government have been required to navigate a system organized around the structure of Government rather than the needs of the people. Americans must search across numerous executive departments and agency (agency) websites, interpret complicated Government terminology, frequently provide the same information, and repeatedly prove their identities to a Government that may already possess the information necessary to serve them. The American people deserve better.
Advances in technology now make possible a fundamentally different relationship between the people and the Federal Government, defined by simplicity, speed, accuracy, security, and respect for the individual. The same spirit of American innovation that can accelerate scientific discovery can also help Americans complete essential interactions with the Federal Government.
This order therefore directs the establishment of America.gov as the unified digital front door to the Federal Government for every individual in the United States seeking Federal information or services. America.gov will not be merely another website, search engine, or directory of Government links. It will be a secure, intelligent, and service-oriented point of entry through which an individual may sign in, communicate in plain language, receive accurate answers, and, where authorized and technically available, complete Government transactions without being required to navigate the websites of multiple agencies. America.gov will enable the Federal Government to do its own paperwork so that the American people may get on with their lives.
Sec. 2. Policy. It is the policy of the United States to:
(a) provide every individual in the United States seeking Federal information or services with a single, secure, conversational point of entry through which the citizen may discover, access, and, where authorized, complete covered Federal transactions;
(b) establish common standards of quality, simplicity, accessibility, interoperability, security, reliability, and design across participating Federal digital services and public-facing websites;
(c) preserve each agency’s custody and control of its records, systems, statutory responsibilities, and adjudicatory authority and ensure that unifying access to Federal services does not create a centralized Federal system of records concerning the American people;
(d) protect personal information through data minimization, secure authentication, auditable authorization, and disclosure practices consistent with applicable law;
(e) ensure that super intelligence used in connection with America.gov is accurate, reliable, and transparent; and
(f) preserve existing lawful methods by which Americans may obtain Federal services, including in-person, telephone, mail, and agency-specific digital services, so that America.gov provides a better option but does not become the only option.
Sec. 3. Definition. The term “covered services” means public-facing Federal services that serve more than 100,000 users in a 12-month period and can be accessed or applied for online. The term excludes tax filing services provided by the Internal Revenue Service and services provided by the Department of War and elements of the Intelligence Community. The Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) may, by memorandum, add or exclude “covered services.”
Sec. 4. Establishing America.gov. The Administrator of General Services, in coordination with the Administrator of the National Design Studio and the Director of OMB, shall:
(a) establish and operate America.gov as the single point of entry for Americans to access covered services online; and
(b) take such steps as are necessary to integrate Login.gov with America.gov, including using Login.gov as the authentication service for America.gov.
Sec. 5. Implementing America.gov. (a) Within 90 days of the date of this order, the Director of OMB shall issue a memorandum to the heads of agencies on implementation of this order.
(b) Heads of agencies shall:
(i) identify covered services in their respective agencies;
(ii) integrate the provisions of such services with America.gov in a secure and privacy-preserving manner, including by making the public Application Programming Interfaces, dashboards, and digital forms that already support services accessible through the America.gov platform;
(iii) complete integration with Login.gov consistent with the requirements of section 1523(b)(1)(D) of title 6, United States Code, and OMB Memorandum M-26-18; and
(iv) provide, on an ongoing basis, the Administrator of General Services and the Director of OMB with historical and current usage and performance data for covered services.
Sec. 6. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect:
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.
(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.
(c) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.
(d) Nothing in this order shall be construed to require the disclosure of information that is prohibited by law, or to authorize any person other than the originating agency to access records maintained by that agency about an individual, except as provided by the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a) or other applicable law.
(e) The costs for publication of this order shall be borne by the General Services Administration.
DONALD J. TRUMP
THE WHITE HOUSE,
September 29, 2026.

sources.news_title: Donald Trump launches new AI government website: What to know
sources.text:
President Donald Trump launched America.gov on Tuesday, unveiling what the administration has billed as a new AI-powered gateway to federal information and services that aims to streamline Americans' interactions with the government.
The website, which Trump introduced at Andrew W. Mellon Auditorium in Washington, features a chatbot-style interface that allows users to ask questions about government programs, benefits and services. The administration described America.gov as a "front door" to federal resources, consolidating information that is currently spread across dozens of agency websites.
"It's not just simply a website. It's a restoration of America's founding promise, and it's a reinvention of your government for the 21st century and beyond," Trump said at the rollout.
The debut of America.gov comes as policymakers, technology companies and privacy advocates continue to debate the expanding role of artificial intelligence in public-facing services. While AI tools have been touted for their ability to simplify complex tasks and improve access to information, experts have raised concerns about accuracy, transparency and data privacy, particularly when such systems are used to help people access government programs or services.
Asked at the announcement about risks associated with AI and centralized government services, Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Administrator Mehmet Oz told Newsweek the administration does not want all user data stored in a single location. Instead, he described America.gov as a "federated system" in which individuals maintain control of their own records and choose whether to share them. Oz acknowledged that any system allowing access to sensitive information carries risks, but said federal officials are prioritizing cybersecurity and data protection as the platform evolves.
"We don't want all the information in one link," Oz said. "The real risk we have is if all your data is in one spot ... anyone who hacks it gets it all."
The president said Tuesday, "It cannot in theory be hacked into. And when they figure a way to do that, we'll end it, because they always figure a way, right?"
Joe Gebbia, U.S. chief design officer, said America.gov is powered by Google's Gemini and Elon Musk's Grok. Trump was joined by Musk, administration officials and tech leaders for the announcement.
Newsweek has reached out to the White House via email on Tuesday morning for comment.
What Trump's America.gov Executive Order Does
Trump signed an executive order Tuesday that directs federal agencies to integrate their online services with America.gov, which the administration envisions as a single digital portal for accessing government information and completing transactions.
The White House said the platform will eventually allow users to perform tasks such as renewing passports and enrolling in Medicare, while Login.gov, the federal government's existing sign-in system, will be incorporated into the service.
The order applies to public-facing federal services used by more than 100,000 people annually, although IRS tax-filing services and certain national security-related functions are excluded.
"This is the American government working for the American people. Come to America.gov, tell us what you need. We'll help you get there and, ultimately, we'll help you get it done," Edward Forst, Administrator of the U.S. General Services Administration (GSA), told Newsweek at Tuesday's announcement.
Expert Warns of Risks Alongside Benefits
Nicol Turner Lee, a senior fellow and director of the Center for Technology Innovation at the Brookings Institution, said AI could help simplify a federal bureaucracy that often requires people to navigate multiple websites and eligibility requirements.
"Using AI, in theory, could help alleviate some of that burden and enable people to find information relevant to their circumstances faster and more easily," she told Newsweek via email, adding that the technology could free federal workers to focus on other tasks.
"However, users will need accountability when something goes wrong to ensure Americans do not bear the burden of missing out on government services if AI fails," Turner Lee continued.
Turner Lee also warned against replacing traditional forms of government assistance with AI-driven tools.
"AI-powered services should not be a replacement for humans who are there to help Americans get the necessary information and access to services," she said, arguing that agencies should carefully evaluate whether artificial intelligence is the most effective method for delivering specific government services.
"When it comes to government services, the results of this could be devastating if Americans miss a deadline, misunderstand eligibility, or are fed misinformation."
Who Is Joe Gebbia?
The launch of America.gov also highlights the growing influence of Gebbia, the Airbnb co-founder whom Trump tapped in 2025 to lead the newly created National Design Studio. Established under the administration's "America by Design" initiative, the office is responsible for modernizing federal websites and digital services.
The chatbot-based America.gov portal represents one of the most visible examples of Gebbia's effort to apply Silicon Valley-style design principles to the federal government.
Testing America.gov
- In a test of the platform, America.gov responded to a question about disabled veterans' benefits with a detailed breakdown of available VA programs, including disability compensation, health care, vocational rehabilitation and housing assistance. The chatbot cited official government resources and linked directly to VA webpages, providing a level of specificity comparable to a traditional agency help page but in a conversational format.
- In another test, America.gov handled a more complex, real-world scenario involving a move from New York to Virginia. Rather than providing a generic answer, the chatbot explained that there is currently no single federal address-change system and walked through the steps required to update records with multiple agencies, including the U.S. Postal Service, IRS, Social Security Administration and Department of Veterans Affairs. It also distinguished between federal and state responsibilities, directing users to Virginia agencies for matters such as driver's licenses and taxes. The response included numerous links to official government resources and concluded by noting that America.gov plans to eventually offer a centralized address-update function, illustrating the administration's vision for the platform as more than just an informational chatbot.
- When asked whether a 12-year-old could enroll in Medicare, the chatbot correctly responded that children generally are not eligible for the program, before outlining a narrow exception for minors with end-stage renal disease whose families meet certain eligibility requirements. It also pointed users toward Medicaid and the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) as more common sources of coverage for children, while linking to official Medicare and Social Security resources. The response suggested the system can provide nuanced answers to unusual questions rather than simply defaulting to a generic explanation of Medicare eligibility.
- The America.gov chatbot provided direct answers Tuesday to a series of questions about the 2020 election, presidential term limits, impeachment proceedings and other politically sensitive topics when Newsweek tested the system shortly after its debut. Newsweek submitted 15 prompts to the chatbot between 12:54 p.m. and 1:06 p.m. ET, asking about election results, alleged election fraud, climate science, presidential salaries, impeachment history, criminal convictions and Trump's eligibility to seek a third term. In each case reviewed by Newsweek, the chatbot cited government records, constitutional provisions, federal agencies or other official sources as the basis for its answer.
Tech Titans Gather at White House for AI Summit
The launch of America.gov coincided with a high-profile White House gathering of some of the technology industry's most influential executives.
Trump hosted a lunch focused on AI shortly after unveiling the new portal Attendees include Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, OpenAI co-founder Greg Brockman, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora and Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner.
The technology leaders joined Vice President JD Vance, House Speaker Mike Johnson, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles. The meeting comes as artificial intelligence is playing an increasingly prominent role in both the private and public sectors, with governments around the world grappling with how to harness the technology while addressing concerns about accuracy, privacy and security.
Later Tuesday, Trump said the major artificial intelligence companies had agreed to a voluntary framework featuring internal and external reviews.
“I think I’m seeing tremendous self-policing. And they understand that they have to self-police,” Trump told reporters outside the West Wing.
Amodei, one of the technology industry's most prominent advocates for slowing the pace of AI development, warned that the technology carries "very real risks."
"The mechanism, how we address those risks, is still under discussion," Amodei said.
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said the voluntary accord establishes a framework for internal safeguards and independent oversight, including audits designed to identify potential problems with AI systems.
"We're going to have all of our boards of directors independently review the reports that come from the auditors," Zuckerberg said.
Trump said the agreement would include a committee of roughly 10 people tasked with overseeing compliance and described the accord as "morally binding." The president added that he expects to name an individual to oversee the initiative in the coming days following consultations with industry leaders.
Newsweek’s reporters and editors used Martyn, our AI assistant, to produce this story. Learn more about Martyn here.
Contact Newsweek editors on this story: Gabe Whisnant and Dave Siminoff.

What it does (and what it doesn’t)
America.gov’s initial capabilities focus on the kind of paperwork that makes people dread interacting with their government. Full Medicare enrollment functionality is expected to come online within the next year.
The executive order requires federal agencies to fast-track integration of their public-facing services into the platform, with a specific threshold: any service that handles more than 100,000 users annually needs to get on board.
IRS tax filing and certain national-security functions are explicitly excluded from the initiative.
The site is free, ad-free, and doesn’t require login credentials for basic usage.
